name: autogen-studio
summary: Visual multi-agent orchestration tooling for designing and operating AutoGen-based workflows.
why_it_matters: The capability is still relevant as future Vrooli scenarios may want visual agent debugging or composition surfaces, but the old registry-only entry was not an actively validated integration.
when_to_use: A future scenario needs a visual UI for building or inspecting multi-agent workflows.
Operators need to compare Vrooli-native orchestration with AutoGen-style agent graph tooling.
An implementation effort wants to prototype agent interaction UX before committing to a maintained integration.

platform_support.notes: The capability likely depends on Python and UI packaging choices, so future support should be explicit about install and runtime assumptions.

prerequisites: Validated demand for an AutoGen-specific operator surface
Clear support boundary relative to Vrooli-native agent tooling
implementation_notes: Treat this as capability knowledge, not an implied endorsement of a specific historical wrapper.
A future promotion should start from explicit install and detection semantics rather than registry metadata alone.
Support should only land if a scenario concretely benefits from the UI.
operational_notes: Desktop-app support should report unsupported platforms honestly.
Future implementations need a crisp story for config storage and operator auth context.
risks: UI-heavy tooling can create maintenance cost without becoming core platform capability.
The AutoGen ecosystem may shift faster than Vrooli should commit to supporting.
